counterfactual_missing_items: No raw evidence of a discrete malignancy, mass, or tissue diagnosis to fully confirm cancer-associated thrombosis
No schistocytes, thrombocytopenia, or prolonged clotting times to support DIC/TTP
Procoagulant and vasculitic studies are negative, disconfirming APS and cerebral vasculitis
decisive_items: Multiple small foci of restricted diffusion in the anterior, middle, and posterior cerebral artery territories
response.rationale: R3 best integrates the otherwise unexplained elevated tumor markers with a hypercoagulable, embolic, multi-territory stroke pattern (elevated D-dimer, multiple arterial-territory infarcts, cardiac echogenic targets), whereas R2 explains D-dimer/fibrinogen and microinfarcts but lacks the tumor/immune cause and is less compatible with elevated fibrinogen and absent schistocytes; R1 and R4 are directly contradicted by negative procoagulant/vasculitic studies; R5 relies on rouleaux/auto-agglutination that are not TTP morphology and conflicts with Coombs-positive AIHA.

rejected.why: No raw support spans and direct contradiction by negative procoagulant studies
Negative vasculitic studies directly contradict cerebral vasculitis; rouleaux/auto-agglutination and tumor markers unexplained
Blood film shows rouleaux/auto-agglutination, not schistocytes; Coombs-positive AIHA and elevated fibrinogen are inconsistent with TTP
